increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

tools/argus/README.md documents what the collector now accepts and serves, and tools/argus/test/CLAUDE.md and tools/argus/CLAUDE.md are current for the cases and modules this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.
skills/agent-brief/assets/CLAUDE.md is current for the cases and helpers this increment adds, in the same commit as the change.

return.summary: Render every recorded step in the run view as a native <details> row - label, preview and time collapsed, the whole return expanded - entirely inside public/run.js and styles.css, leaving app.js, index.html and format.js untouched.
return.plan:
WHAT GETS BUILT Every step the backlog holds becomes a row in the run view: the steps recorded against each increment, inside that increment's card, and the run's own steps (`state.run.steps` - the opening cut, each close, the publish) in a panel of their own. A row is a native `
`: the `` is the collapsed line (label, a one-line preview, the time), and the body is the whole return, pretty-printed JSON in a `
`. All of it lands in tools/argus-ui/public/run.js and its styling in tools/argus-ui/public/styles.css. No other production file changes - see the module map for why app.js, index.html and format.js stay untouched.

THE WIRE SHAPE THIS RENDERS (verified against skills/agent-brief/assets/backlog.mjs and tools/argus/src/store.mjs)

The recorder writes each step as `{ label, at, return }` where `at` is an ISO-8601 string (`new Date().toISOString()`) and `return` is the agent's whole structured return - any JSON value. `close()` sheds them: a closed increment gets `steps: []`, and every entry in `run.steps` keeps `label` and `at` with the `return` key deleted outright. The collector stores the document opaquely (`putRunState` reads only `issue`, `workflow` and `increments.length`) and `GET /api/runs/:id` serves the entry with `state` whole, so the steps arrive exactly as the recorder wrote them. Nothing truncates them on the way. Two shed shapes therefore both have to render: an increment with an empty `steps` array, and a run step object with no `return` key at all.

WHAT TO ADD TO public/run.js

1. `import { esc, fmtAgo, previewOf } from './format.js';` - `previewOf` and `PREVIEW_CHARS` already exist in format.js (120 chars, ellipsis when cut), so no formatter is added.

2. `export const STEP_SHED_NOTE = 'return shed at close';` - the line a step with no `return` key shows in place of a preview. Without it that row renders a blank cell, which reads as broken; the recorder's own doc calls this shedding, so the page says the same word.

3. `export function stepView(step)` - the pure derivation, so the suite can test the reading of a step apart from its markup. Returns `{ label, at, timeMs, hasReturn, text, preview }`:
   - `label`: `typeof step?.label === 'string' ? step.label : ''`.
   - `at`: `typeof step?.at === 'string' ? step.at : ''` (kept verbatim for the `data-at` attribute).
   - `timeMs`: `Date.parse(at)` when finite, else `0`. Zero is deliberate: `fmtAgo(0)` returns `'never'`, so an unparseable or missing instant can never print `NaN`.
   - `hasReturn`: `Object.hasOwn(entry, 'return') && entry.return !== undefined`. The key's presence is the test, not truthiness - a return of `null`, `0`, `''` or `false` is a return that was recorded and must render as one.
   - `text`: the whole return as text - the string itself when the return is a string, else `JSON.stringify(value, null, 2)`, inside a try/catch falling back to `String(value)`. `''` when `hasReturn` is false.
   - `preview`: `previewOf(summary || text)` where `summary` is `entry.return.summary` when the return is a plain object carrying a non-empty string there, else the flattened text. `STEP_SHED_NOTE` when `hasReturn` is false. Preferring the return's own `summary` field is what makes the collapsed line readable - every uroboros agent return carries one - and falling back to the serialised text is what makes a return of any other shape still show something.

4. `export function renderSteps(steps)` - `''` for a missing, non-array or empty list, else `
    ` of one `
  1. ` per step, in the array's own order (map, never sort). Returning the empty string is what satisfies the "no empty panel" criterion: a shed increment's card renders exactly as it does today.

5. A file-local `renderStep(step)`: builds `stepView` and emits

   `
  2. ………` + (`hasReturn` ? `
    …
    ` : `''`) + `
    3. `

   Every printed value goes through `esc`; the `data-at` value goes through the existing file-local `attr()` helper, for the same reason `data-run` does - a hostile document must not be able to spell a second attribute. The `
    ` is left off entirely when nothing was recorded, so no empty box appears under a shed row.

6. `renderIncrement` gains `${renderSteps(increment?.steps)}` as its last child, after the note.

7. `renderRun` gains the run's own steps between the increments list and the codemap:
   - read them defensively - `held.run && typeof held.run === 'object' && Array.isArray(held.run.steps) ? held.run.steps : []`;
   - when non-empty, emit `
    Run steps
    ${renderSteps(runSteps)}
    `, mirroring the codemap panel that already sits there;
   - when empty, emit nothing.
   The head, the chips, the counts, the increment cards, the codemap and the empty states are not otherwise touched.

STYLING (public/styles.css, appended to the run-view section that ends with `.run-codemap pre`)

`.run-steps` (list-style none, no padding, small top margin), `.run-step` (a hairline `border-top: 1px solid var(--border)` so rows read as a list), `.run-step > details > summary` (grid `160px 1fr auto`, baseline aligned, `cursor: pointer`, `list-style: none` plus the `::-webkit-details-marker { display: none }` rule the ctx blocks already use), `.run-step-label` (mono, 11px, accent), `.run-step-preview` (`min-width: 0; overflow: hidden; text-overflow: ellipsis; white-space: nowrap` - this is what keeps a very long return on one line when collapsed), `.run-step-time` (mono, 10px, faint, right aligned), `.run-step-return` (`max-height: 50vh; overflow: auto; white-space: pre-wrap; word-break: break-word`, mono 11px, sunken background - modelled on `.ctx-text`, and what keeps one enormous return from burying the increments under it), `.run-steps-panel` and `.run-steps-head` (the same uppercase micro-heading as `.run-codemap-head`). Every one of these class names must appear in a `class="…"` attribute in run.js, or the page suite's "no class the stylesheet styles is one no source can emit" case goes red.

DOCUMENTATION (implementer's, in the same commit)

- tools/argus-ui/README.md: the opening description (the paragraph under `# argus-ui`, above `## Quick start`) still enumerates only sessions, timeline and context - add the uroboros runs it holds, so the intro agrees with "What it shows". Extend the existing **Runs** bullet with the steps: each increment's recorded steps and the run's own steps, each collapsed to a line carrying its label and time and expanding to the whole return, and that a closed increment shows none because the recorder sheds them. Do not use the word "tab" anywhere in the file - a page suite case bans `/\btabs?\b/i` in every .md under tools/argus-ui.
- tools/argus-ui/CLAUDE.md: the "No build step and no framework" bullet describes run.js as the run view; extend that one sentence to say it renders the steps too. Nothing else there is stale.
- tools/argus-ui/test/CLAUDE.md is the test-author's, not the implementer's.

DECISIONS TAKEN, AND WHAT WAS REJECTED

- Native `
    `, with no open-state tracking in app.js. Rejected: mirroring the context panel's `state.expanded` set - a new state field, a delegated click listener on `#run-detail` (which has none today), an `expanded` argument through `renderRun`, and page-suite guards for all of it. It buys only that an expanded step survives a live repaint, which no criterion asks for, and run frames arrive once per recorder write (minutes apart), not per second. The cost is a page-wide wiring change to an increment that otherwise touches one module. Consequence to accept knowingly: a live write to the shown run collapses any step the reader had opened.
- The whole return is shown as pretty-printed JSON in a `
    `, not as a field-by-field rendering. The collector holds the document opaquely and a return has no fixed schema; a per-field renderer would teach the page a shape it cannot rely on, and the criterion asks for "the full return", which the serialised text is.
- The collapsed line prefers the return's own `summary` string and falls back to the flattened serialisation. Rejected: always serialising, which makes every line read `{ "plan": "WHAT GETS BUILT\n\nEvery step…` and tells a reader nothing.
- The run's own steps sit in one panel after the increments and before the codemap, not interleaved with them. The backlog holds them under `run`, not under any increment, and showing them inside a card would attribute a close or a publish to whichever increment it landed near.
- `renderSteps` returns the empty string rather than a placeholder for an empty list. A closed increment having no steps is the recorder working as designed, so the card should read as an ordinary closed card - which is exactly what the criterion asks for.
- Step time is rendered with the existing `fmtAgo`, over `Date.parse` of the ISO string, with `0` for anything unparseable. Rejected: adding a formatter to format.js - it already carries everything needed, as the ui increment also found.

New fixture for run.test.mjs, beside the existing four:
`const step = (over = {}) => ({ label: 'research:ui', at: new Date(Date.now() - 60_000).toISOString(), return: { summary: 'a short summary line' }, ...over });`
A shed run step is written as `(() => { const { return: _drop, ...rest } = step(); return rest; })()` or by `delete`-ing the key - the key must be absent, not set to undefined, because that is what the recorder's `close` leaves behind.

CASES — run.test.mjs (unit; run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/run.test.mjs`)

Criterion: each increment shows the steps recorded against it, in the backlog's order, each with label, time and return.
1. "an increment's steps render in the backlog's own order, each with its label, its instant and its return". Input: one increment carrying three steps with labels `research:x`, `tests:x`, `impl:x`, three distinct `at` instants, and returns whose `summary` fields are distinct markers. State: `runEntry({ state: doc({ increments: [that increment] }) })`. Expect: `renderRun` output contains all three labels; `html.indexOf` proves the three in the fixture's order (prove the fixture non-vacuous by asserting the three markers differ); each step's ISO instant appears as `data-at="<iso>"` (assert the attribute, not a locale-formatted string); the number of `<li class="run-step"` occurrences is exactly 3.
2. "the collapsed line shows a preview and the expanded body shows the whole return". Input: a step whose return is `{ summary: 'short summary', plan: 'a marker only the body may carry' }`. Expect: the summary text appears inside the `<summary>…</summary>` slice, the plan marker appears in the `<pre class="run-step-return">` slice and not in the summary slice, and the markup carries `<details` and `</details>` around both.
3. "a very long return collapses to one line and still opens to the whole of it". Input: a step whose return is a single string of 5000 `x` characters (no `summary` field to prefer). Expect: the `<summary>` slice is far shorter than the return - assert the rendered preview is at most `PREVIEW_CHARS + 1` characters and ends with the ellipsis - while the `<pre>` slice contains the full 5000-character run. No `undefined`, no `NaN`.
4. "a return of any shape renders, and none of them prints undefined or NaN". Input: one increment carrying five steps whose returns are, in turn: an object missing the `summary` field, an object with nested objects and arrays (assert a leaf value from three levels down reaches the `<pre>`), `null`, the number `0`, and a bare string. Expect: `renderRun` does not throw, every step renders a row, and the whole output contains neither `undefined` nor `NaN`.
5. "a step whose return was shed still renders its label and its time, with no return body". Input: a run step object carrying `label` and `at` and no `return` key. Expect: the label and the `data-at` value are present; `STEP_SHED_NOTE` is on the line; the output contains no `run-step-return` for that row; no `undefined`.
6. "an increment the backlog holds with no steps renders as the ordinary card it is". Input: `increment({ id: 'closed-one', status: 'done', note: 'accepted', steps: [] })` and a second increment with `steps` missing entirely. Expect: both cards render with their id, title, status and note; the output contains no `run-steps` list and no `run-step` row at all; no `undefined`, no `NaN`; the closed card still carries `data-closed="true"` (the existing behaviour must not regress).

Criterion: the run's own steps appear in the same view and read the same way.
7. "the run's own steps render in the order the backlog holds them, in a panel of their own". Input: `doc({ run: { steps: [step({label:'cut'}), step({label:'close:ui'}), step({label:'publish'})] } })` with one increment that has no steps. Expect: all three labels present in that order; they render with the same `run-step` / `run-step-label` / `run-step-return` classes the increment steps use; and they sit outside the increment cards - assert `html.indexOf('run-increments') < html.indexOf('run-steps-panel')`, and that the substring from `run-increments` up to `run-steps-panel` contains no `run-step-label`, which proves the three labels landed in the panel and not in the step-less card above it.
8. "a document carrying no run steps renders no run-steps panel". Inputs, each its own assertion in one case: `doc({ run: { steps: [] } })`, `doc({ run: null })`, `doc({ run: 'not an object' })`, and a document with the `run` key absent. Expect for each: `renderRun` does not throw, the output contains no `run-steps-panel`, and contains neither `undefined` nor `NaN`. The head, the counts and the codemap still render (assert the codemap text is still there, so the case proves the panel was skipped and not the whole tail).

Criterion: a step return of any shape renders and nothing crashes or leaks - the `stepView` derivation behind it.
9. "stepView reads a step's label, instant and return, and never yields NaN". Input: `step()` - expect `label`, `at` verbatim, `timeMs === Date.parse(at)`, `hasReturn === true`, a non-empty `preview`. Inputs `step({ at: '' })`, `step({ at: 'not a date' })` and `step({ at: undefined })` - expect `timeMs === 0` for each, and that rendering such a step prints `fmtAgo(0)` (which is `never`) and no `NaN`. Input `stepView(undefined)` and `stepView(null)` - expect an object with empty `label`, `timeMs === 0` and `hasReturn === false`, never a throw.
10. "a return recorded as null, 0, empty string or false is a return, not a shed one". Input: four steps with those four returns. Expect `stepView(...).hasReturn === true` for each and a `run-step-return` body rendered for each; `STEP_SHED_NOTE` appears nowhere in that markup. This is the edge that a truthiness test instead of a key test would fail.
11. "everything a step prints is escaped". Input: a step with label `<script>alert(1)</script>`, `at` `2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z" onmouseover="x`, and a return carrying `<script>` and both quote kinds. Expect: no raw `<script` in the output, and no `onmouseover=` in the output (the `data-at` attribute cannot be broken out of).

Criterion: switching runs and a live write leave only the steps of the state now shown.
12. "a rendered run carries the steps of the entry it was given and of no other". Input: two entries A and B, each with a distinct step label in an increment and a distinct label in `run.steps`. Expect: `renderRun(A)` contains A's two labels and neither of B's, and the reverse for `renderRun(B)`. This is the unit half; the page half is case 13.

CASES — page.test.mjs (source text; run with `node --test tools/argus-ui/test/page.test.mjs`)

13. "the run pane is repainted wholesale from the state the page holds". Read public/app.js, slice `renderRunView` with `functionSource`, assert it matches `/container\.innerHTML\s*=\s*renderRun\(state\.run\)/` - a replacement rather than an append is what leaves no step of the previous state on the page after a switch or a live write. Assert too that `selectRun` and `refreshRuns` each still call `renderRunView(` (both already do; state the case is green before the change and is a guard, not a new red).
14. "the stylesheet styles a step collapsed to a line and expanded to its whole return". Read public/styles.css and assert it includes `.run-steps`, `.run-step-label`, `.run-step-preview`, `.run-step-time` and `.run-step-return`; assert the `.run-step-return` rule's own block carries `max-height` and `overflow`, so one enormous return cannot bury the increments. Read public/run.js and assert each of those class names is emitted in a `class="…"` attribute there. (The existing "no class the stylesheet styles is one no source can emit" case guards the other direction and must stay green.)
15. "README.md's opening description names the runs the interface shows". Read tools/argus-ui/README.md, slice from the `# argus-ui` heading to the first `##` heading, assert that slice matches `/\bruns\b/i`. Non-vacuous today: that slice says "run on the machine you are sitting at" in the singular and carries no plural "runs", so this case is red before the change.
16. "README.md says the run view shows each step, collapsed and expandable". Read tools/argus-ui/README.md and assert it matches `/\bsteps?\b/i` and `/expand/i`. Keep the existing README case (run, increment, status, codemap) untouched beside it.

WHAT IS LEFT UNTESTED, AND WHY

- That a browser actually opens and shuts a `<details>`. There is no DOM in this suite by design (test/CLAUDE.md), and the element's native behaviour is the platform's, not this code's. What is testable - that the collapsed line and the full return are both in the markup, in the right halves of one `<details>` - is case 2.
- That an expanded step survives a live repaint. It does not, by decision (see the plan), and no criterion asks for it.
- Live delivery of a run frame end to end. It is the previous increment's, already covered by page.test.mjs's `connectStream` and `refreshRuns` cases and by run.test.mjs's `shouldLoadRun` cases; this increment adds no wiring to it.
- The collector's own storing and serving of `run.steps`. Settled in the collector increment and covered by tools/argus/test; the state is stored opaquely, so nothing here can change it.
- tools/argus-ui/test/independence.test.mjs gains no case: this increment adds no module, and its three explicit scans already name `public/run.js`.

WHAT IS ALREADY RED

I ran nothing. From reading: both suites are green as they stand (the ui increment closed with both green). Every case above except 13 is red until the implementation lands - 13 is a guard over code that already exists and passes now.

increments.title: The collector accepts, keeps, persists, serves and announces a run's state
increments.goal: Give the collector an endpoint of its own that accepts a run's backlog state, keep the latest state per run, serve the runs it holds and the full state of one over its JSON API behind the existing authentication, persist it across a restart, and announce every write on the existing SSE stream.
criteria: A POST of a run's state to an endpoint of the collector's own is accepted and identified by the issue the state belongs to; a second POST for the same run replaces what was held for it, so the collector keeps the latest state per run and no history.

The JSON API answers both questions: the runs the collector holds, with what a reader needs to pick one including when each was last written, and the full state of one named run; asking for a run it does not hold answers 404.
The new ingest endpoint and the new read endpoints sit behind the collector's existing authentication and reject an unauthenticated caller exactly as its other endpoints do.
A collector restarted against the same measurement directory still serves the run state it held, persisted the way the sessions it already holds are persisted.
A write to a run's state puts a frame on the existing /api/stream SSE stream that tells an already-connected client which run changed.

increments.title: The recorder pushes the state it just wrote, best-effort and invisible
increments.goal: Make the recorder send the run's state to the configured collector after every write it makes, without changing anything an agent or a workflow sees and without ever costing a run a failure, a wait or a line of output.
criteria: init, record, branch and close each send the state they just wrote to the collector's run-state endpoint, identified by the issue the state belongs to, so a collector that receives it then serves that exact document under that issue.
The recorder stays the only writer of backlog.json and keeps its zero dependencies; no agent page and no workflow prompt changes, so how an agent calls the recorder is exactly what it is today.
The collector's address and its credential are read from the same OTLP collector environment the rest of uroboros already exports for argus, and from nowhere else.
With no collector configured in the environment, the recorder does nothing extra.

A collector that is unreachable, slow or refusing costs the recorder neither a non-zero exit nor a wait beyond a short timeout, and produces no output: the exit codes and the one confirmation line of every subcommand stay byte-identical to today's.

increments.title: argus-ui gains a run view: one run's backlog, switchable and live
increments.goal: Give the interface a run view beside its session view that shows a run's backlog as the collector serves it, opens on the most recently written run, lets the reader switch runs, and updates itself over the collector's SSE stream.
criteria: The interface shows a run view beside its existing session view, holding for the run it shows: the issue and the workflow it belongs to and when it was last written; the increments in the backlog's order, each with its id, title, status, branch and note; a count of how many increments are closed and how many are open; and the codemap.
A closed increment reads as closed, with its status and its note.

The view opens on the run written to most recently and the reader can switch to any other run the collector holds, taking both the list of runs and the one run's whole state from the collector's run endpoints and from no other source.

A write to the shown run's state reaches an already-open page live over the collector's Server-Sent-Events stream, whose frame names only which run changed and when: no polling, no reload, no manual refresh.
The existing session view, its timeline and its stream handling keep working unchanged beside the new view.
